snapshot_markdown:
**Ioneer Ltd (ASX: INR)** — Lithium-Boron Mining Development. North Sydney, NSW with Reno, Nevada office. 23 employees. Founded 2001. Sole asset: **Rhyolite Ridge Lithium-Boron Project, Nevada, USA.** Construction approval received Oct 2025, US District Court upheld approval Mar 30, 2026. Boron added to US Critical Minerals List Nov 6, 2025.

## Situational read
This is the cleanest construction-phase mining prospect we've seen. INR has done what most ASX-listed development-stage miners cannot: get a US federal lithium-boron project across the finish line of approval. They have $25M cash, $230M equity book, $434M of accumulated PIPE capital, and a cap table that includes **Sibanye-Stillwater** (PGM major), **BNP Paribas**, **Centaurus Capital**, and **Bank of New York Mellon** (though BNY just reduced position).

But the operating context is hostile. In 6 months: CFO departed (Sep 21, 2025), construction approval landed (Oct 19, market sold off 7%), governance changes (Oct 24, -3%), interim CFO without permanent backfill (Nov 10, -3%), executive reshuffling (Dec 1), and then a $50M January 2026 capital raise that the market punished -24% in a single session and -32.6% on the month. BNY Mellon reduced position Feb 8 (-5%). The Mar 30 court win bounced 7% but did not restore prior valuation.

MD Bernard Rowe's compensation tripled in 2025 ($972K to $2.63M). SVP Matt Weaver's compensation nearly doubled ($813K to $1.53M). Boards do not pay those numbers to maintain status quo. The 23-person team that ran the permitting fight is not the team that runs a $400M+ construction project. **That is the gap. And it is open right now.**

## Capital structure
**$434.39M raised across 14 disclosed rounds.** Heavy institutional cap table. Key rounds: Feb 2026 PIPE $49.09M (Rhyolite Ridge acceleration, shares -24%), Jul/Jun 2025 PIPEs totaling $34.63M, Sep 2021 $70M led by Sibanye-Stillwater, Mar 2021 $62.17M led by BNP Paribas. Zero commercial debt — construction-phase project finance structure still to be built.

**Warning flag:** Bank of New York Mellon reduced position Feb 8, 2026 (shares -5%). Institutional confidence wobble.

## Recent activity (last 6 months)
Oct 19, 2025: Construction approval (BLM) — shares fell 7%. Nov 6: Boron added to US Critical Minerals List. Nov 10: Interim CFO (shares -3%). Dec 1: Executive changes. Dec 12: AFR reports Rio Tinto US boron unit acquisition rumor. Jan 29, 2026: $50M placement — shares plunged 24%. Feb 8: BNY Mellon reduces stake (-5%). Mar 30: US District Court upholds Nevada project (+7%).

## Top contacts for outreach
**Primary target: Bernard Rowe** (MD/CEO, browe@ioneer.com, +61 2 9922 5800). Compensation tripled in 2025. Pitch: "You cleared the federal hurdles. The team that got you through permitting is not the team that runs the build."

**Secondary: Matt Weaver** (SVP, $1.53M comp in 2025). Confirm portfolio via LinkedIn — if he runs Nevada operations, he is the implementation buyer.

**Board escalation: James Calaway** (Chairman, since Jan 2017). Self-representing, holds institutional memory.

**Do NOT lead with: April Hashimoto** (interim CFO). Finance function is sensitive — permanent search likely still active.

## Why they'd buy
23-person team, $434M raised, court-cleared construction mandate, and a CFO hole. New Delta entry points: construction-phase org design and hiring sequence; LTO posture for BLM monitoring + state water rights + DOE loan compliance; strategic-investor governance for Sibanye-Stillwater board cadence; M&A integration readiness if Rio Tinto boron acquisition proceeds; 2-year production roadmap working backward from first lithium-boron output.

**Tier: A-tier.** Cleanest construction-phase development prospect in the funnel. First-touch to Bernard Rowe within 4-6 weeks while Jan-Feb 2026 dilution shock and Mar 30 court ruling are both fresh.
